title: Fed Policy Twist May Trigger ETF Rotation Away From Floating-Rate Funds
author: Chandrima Sanyal
description: Federal Reserve Governor Stephen Miran's proposal to shrink the balance sheet while potentially allowing lower rates threatens the investment thesis of floating-rate bank loan ETFs. These funds have thrived in a high-rate environment, but falling rates would reduce their income generation, potentially triggering a rotation toward duration-sensitive fixed-income ETFs. While liquidity improvements could provide some support through price stability, the shift challenges the 'higher for longer' narrative that has driven bank loan ETF performance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Faces headwinds from potential rate cuts which would reduce floating coupon income. While liquidity improvements offer some support through price stability, the core investment thesis of higher yields is threatened.
Similar to BKLN, this bank loan ETF would experience reduced income generation if rates fall, despite potential benefits from improved liquidity and credit market support.
Floating-rate structure means coupons will decline with lower rates, offering little price appreciation potential compared to fixed-rate alternatives.
Fixed-rate bond ETF that would benefit from potential rate declines as existing higher-coupon bonds appreciate in value, making it an attractive rotation target.
Duration-sensitive ETF that would benefit significantly from lower rates, making it an attractive destination for investors rotating out of floating-rate funds.
